solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Excursion from French city cut short

indicators.note: a word cut short loses its final letter, so the city name drops its tail

parts.note: Tours is a city on the Loire in France

explanation.surface: A day trip that leaves a French city but has to be curtailed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' removes the last letter, S, from TOURS.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a trip taken for pleasure, visiting several places, is an excursion.

clue.text: Turn down quantity of filled dumplings

parts.note: to turn down lights is to dim them
a sum is an amount or quantity

explanation.surface: Someone refusing a serving of stuffed dumplings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn down' looks like refusing, but it means lowering lights.
explanation.definitionFit: Dim sum are small Chinese steamed parcels with savoury fillings, so they are filled dumplings.

clue.text: Interference to broadcast around the north

indicators.note: the scattering word is placed around the compass letter, enclosing it

parts.note: to broadcast seed is to scatter it, to sow
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: Signal interference to a radio broadcast in the north of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' reads as transmission, but here it is the farming sense of scattering seed.
explanation.definitionFit: Speckled visual interference on an analogue television picture is called snow.

parts.note: a scut is the short tail of a rabbit or deer

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each of the words 'of' and 'rabbit'

explanation.surface: An instruction to cut off a rabbit's tail first of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snip' looks like a verb, but it is a nickname for a clothes-maker, who snips cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Snip is an informal nickname for a maker of suits, from the cutting of cloth.

definitions.meaning: to disregard or dismiss something as unimportant

explanation.surface: Ignore the cut.
explanation.definitionFit: To disregard a claim is to discount it, and a markdown in price is also a discount.

indicators.note: condemned suggests something wrecked or ruined, so these letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A military trainee condemned as a coward hears the cry go up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'condemned' rearranges the letters of CRY AS CADET.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal, childish synonym for someone easily frightened, a fearful person.

parts.note: Robin is a boy's name, and a son is a boy
Robin is a boy's name, and a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A soul singer and his two sons.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's means 'is'. Smokey Robinson was the Motown soul singer of the Miracles.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: Smokey Robinson is a famous American soul and Motown vocalist.

indicators.note: unsettled suggests disturbed or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone feeling gloomy while staying somewhere unfamiliar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unsettled' rearranges the letters of STAYING.
explanation.definitionFit: Stygian, from the river Styx of the underworld, means very dark or murky.

definitions.meaning: a piece, slang for a single firearm

explanation.surface: A firearm for every person.
explanation.definitionFit: Split as 'a piece' it is slang for one firearm; as one word it means for every one individually.

parts.note: F is an abbreviation for fellow, as in FRS
hairy is slang for dangerous or risky

explanation.surface: A description of an energetic, shaggy man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hairy' looks like a description of a person, but is slang for dangerous.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: playful and full of energy, like a frolicking young animal.

clue.text: Abrupt dramatist, eccentric and unpredictable type

indicators.note: abrupt here means cut off sharply, so the playwright's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Oscar Wilde was the Irish playwright
a card is an eccentric or amusing person

explanation.surface: A brusque playwright described as odd and unpredictable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abrupt' reads as describing manner, but it docks the E from WILDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild card is someone or something whose behaviour cannot be foreseen.

clue.text: What can make G-man spit in favourite haunt?

parts.note: the letters of 'stamping', when ground up (rearranged), make G-MAN SPIT

explanation.surface: Something that might make an FBI agent spit, found in his usual hangout.
explanation.walkthrough: Reverse clue: STAMPING ground, i.e. scrambled, gives G-MAN SPIT. A G-man is an American FBI agent.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: the place someone habitually frequents is their stamping ground.

clue.text: Machine, pretty faulty having loose wire inside

indicators.note: inside places the second jumble within the first
faulty suggests something not working properly, so these letters are reordered
loose suggests something come apart, so these letters are also jumbled

explanation.surface: A rather broken machine with a loose wire within.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pretty' looks like 'rather', but is fodder for 'faulty'; the jumble of the wire, from 'loose', sits 'inside' it.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the keyboard device that prints letters on paper is a kind of machine.

clue.text: See head of glamour girl in mirror

indicators.note: head of takes the opening letter of 'glamour'

parts.note: lass is a word for a girl

explanation.surface: Watch a glamorous model looking at herself in a mirror.
explanation.definitionFit: A looking-glass is a mirror, so the reflective pane can be called simply a glass.

indicators.note: over signals that the word for blows is turned back to front

parts.note: raps are sharp knocks or blows

explanation.surface: A boxing match in which the punching is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns RAPS around. 'Box' looks like a noun, but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To box in practice without full force, against a partner, is to spar.

definitions.meaning: a fee paid upfront to secure someone's services

explanation.surface: Money paid upfront to engage a servant.
explanation.definitionFit: A fee paid ahead to engage a lawyer is a retainer, and so is a long-serving domestic attendant.

clue.text: Animal seen in many a land

indicators.note: seen in signals the letters are visible within the phrase that follows

explanation.surface: A creature that is spotted in many countries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in' points to letters inside MANY A LAND.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the nyala is a spiral-horned African antelope, a kind of animal.

parts.note: a band is a group or gang
on means working, as a machine that is switched on

explanation.surface: A gang of labourers at work in a desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' looks like a noun, but it is the verb to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to desert someone is to leave them behind for good.

definitions.meaning: a moment, as in 'just a moment'
informal British word for buying now and paying later

explanation.surface: Credit available immediately.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief moment is a tick in British usage, and buying on tick means buying on credit.

clue.text: As well as bagging game, sailor attends club for midnight meeting

indicators.note: bagging means capturing in a bag, so the outer word encloses the rest

parts.note: with means together with, as well as

indicators.note: attends means is beside, so the sailor goes next to the club

parts.note: chess is a board game
AB is able seaman, a sailor
a bat is a club used in games

explanation.surface: A sailor goes to a club at midnight, playing a game too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bagging' splits the word for 'As well as' around everything else, with the sailor and club joined by 'attends'.
explanation.definitionFit: A witches' sabbath is a gathering of witches traditionally held at midnight.

parts.note: a hit is a popular success
man as in 'man and wife', a husband

explanation.surface: A murderer features in a bestselling book written by a husband.
explanation.definitionFit: A hired assassin, paid to murder people, is commonly called this.

clue.text: A couple of lines in poor song

indicators.note: in places the two line letters within the word for poor

parts.note: bad means poor in quality
L is an abbreviation for line, so two lines are LL

explanation.surface: A weak song with just a couple of lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballad is a narrative song or a slow sentimental popular number.

indicators.note: adopted by means taken in by, so the word for home goes inside

parts.note: a nun is called sister
in means at home

explanation.surface: A child left home and was taken in by a nun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like a verb, but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister comes from Latin for the left hand, and in heraldry means the left side.

indicators.note: reportedly means as said by others, so the word is taken as it is spoken

parts.note: a rhyme is a short verse or poem

explanation.surface: A poem said to be by Robert Frost.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's means 'is'. Frost looks like the poet Robert Frost.
explanation.definitionFit: Rime is a coating of ice crystals formed on cold surfaces, a hoar frost.

clue.text: Unhappy about everyone suffering a setback in oil centre

indicators.note: a setback here is a going back, so the whole is read backwards
about means around, so the unhappy word wraps the word for everyone

parts.note: sad means unhappy
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Everyone is gloomy as the oil town suffers a reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering a setback' turns the whole assembly around, not just 'everyone' beside it, giving SALLAD read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the Texan city is famous as a hub of the American petroleum industry.

clue.text: Song from Callas needing no introduction

indicators.note: no introduction means the opening letter of the singer's first name is dropped

parts.note: Maria Callas was the famous opera soprano

explanation.surface: A song from a diva so famous she needs no introduction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing no introduction' drops the first letter, M, from MARIA.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo song in an opera, like those Callas sang.

indicators.note: out means taken away, so the letter for left is removed

parts.note: a general is a senior army officer

explanation.surface: Paperwork the army officer left out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forms' looks like documents, but means kinds or classes.
explanation.definitionFit: Genera are biological classifications, kinds or types, ranking above species.

indicators.note: served suggests something dished up or prepared, so these letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An official was served a dram of whisky in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served' rearranges the letters of A DRAM INN.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandarin was a Chinese imperial official, and now means a powerful senior civil servant.
